title: Context reconciler and low-overhead instrumentation shim for request telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and ship a compact runtime-friendly instrumentation shim ("reconciler") for the Redwood SDKs and edge middleware that: 1) attaches stable, canonical request metadata to every incoming request with minimal allocations; 2) reconciles multiple incoming context carriers (HTTP headers, gRPC metadata, websocket init frames) into a single lightweight in-memory envelope; and 3) exposes an opt-in sampling and tagging hook so downstream services can add low-cardinality attributes for routing and cost attribution without amplifying cardinality in our trace backend.

Goals and scope:
- Provide 0-alloc fast path for existing hot RPC codepaths, with graceful fallback for legacy carriers.
- Ensure deterministic header precedence and a reconciliation policy that prevents duplicate IDs and header injection loops.
- Add a sampling hint API that allows SDK consumers to annotate candidate requests (sample_hint=high/low) which the runtime can use when making adaptive sampler decisions.
- Ship small SDK changes and a backwards-compatible middleware shim to reduce churn for integrators.
- Avoid adding heavyweight dependencies to edge proxies; keep implementation as a single small module per language.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not modify the server-side sampler implementation in the ingest pipeline (follow-up ticket planned).
- It does not add high-cardinality attributes by default.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Envelope model: use a fixed-shape struct (request_id, incoming_carriers, trace_id_hint, sample_hint, arrival_ts) rather than free-form maps to keep memory predictable. This trades some flexibility for lower GC pressure.
- Precedence rules: explicit precedence order (signed header > x-redwood-* > legacy-ctx) to avoid downstream ambiguities. We will implement a header-normalization step that strips known debug-only keys to prevent accidental span inflation.
- Sampler hints: expose string enums ("high", "medium", "low") and a numeric confidence score for advanced callers. Sampler will treat hints as advisory only; enforced sampling changes are out of scope here.
- Failure modes: if conflict detected (different trace IDs across carriers), reconciler will retain the server-generated trace id and attach conflicting values as debug metadata but not surface them as canonical IDs. This avoids trace fragmentation while preserving forensic info.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK shim exists for Node, Go, and Python runtimes; provides the envelope API and middleware glue.
2) End-to-end latency increase <= 0.2ms P50 on our micro-bench harness for the Node hot path; memory overhead <= 1 extra object per request on average.
3) Fuzz tests for carrier merging and precedence rules added to SDK test suites.
4) Integration tests that demonstrate consistent trace_id and stable sampling hint propagation across an example request flow (edge -> gateway -> model runtime).
5) Documented migration guide and one-page design doc linked from the ticket.

Implementation plan (phased):
- Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype reconciler in Go (shared design), microbench baseline, and spec. Produce design doc and open RFC in our docs repo (Confluence link below).
- Phase 2 (SDK work, 2 weeks): implement shim in Node and Go SDKs. Add middleware integration for Express/gRPC. Add tests and metrics.
- Phase 3 (language parity, 1 week): lightweight Python shim and test matrix.
- Phase 4 (rollout, 1 week): release SDK minor versions with opt-in flag, coordinate with infra for staged rollout and feature flag toggle.

Metrics and dashboards to update:
- Add new telemetry: reconciler.hits, reconciler.conflicts, reconciler.fallbacks, sampler.hint.received.{high,medium,low}. These are counters.
- Latency histogram for reconciler.local_ns in the SDK metrics export.
- Dashboard: Observability -> Tracing -> "Request Reconciler" panel showing conflict rate and P50/P95 reconciliation latency per region and per SDK version.
- Alert: if reconciler.conflicts > 0.1% of requests for 5m, page on-call.

Rollout and compatibility:
- Default behavior during rollout is opt-in. We will coordinate with internal partners and announce SDK previews. After 4 weeks and no major issues, flip rollout to on by default behind a runtime feature flag.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Context+Reconciler+RFC
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pulls/1428 (Node prototype branch)
- Microbench dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/microbench/reconciler

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: increased cardinality if integrators misuse the sample_hint API. Mitigation: add vetting and runtime scrubber to block high-cardinality keys and require explicit opt-in for any free-form attributes.
- Risk: backwards-incompatible header normalization. Mitigation: provide a compatibility shim that preserves original headers in debug metadata for 30 days and a compatibility test harness for integrators.

Next steps (short term):
- Finish spike and publish RFC by 2026-02-17.
- Land prototype Go reconciler and microbench PR (ENG-472891-spike branch).
- Schedule design review with Platform Observability and SDK owners (invite list in comments).
